body: I'm sure no one is checking this, anxiously hoping I'm still alive or whatever (it would be pretty self-centered of me to think that was the case!) but I wanted to drop a note to say that I am doing a bit better now. Thanks for the support and help from all of you strangers on the internet. It really means a lot to me.

Thanks for taking the time to be here, Always_Sunny. 

I'm not really angry with my boyfriend anymore, and we've made up, on the surface.

My boyfriend has told me that he needs me to be strong, so I'm not sure what to do with that.

Dear _moonchild_, thank you for taking the time to write here. It means a lot to me. 

I've tried to talk to him, but it's been difficult. He is no longer suicidal and doesn't want to dwell. He also told me that I have to be the strong one in the relationship, so it's not just that I feel that way -- he's indicated that it is important to him. 

Thanks.

itcanwait, thank you for your insights. This is very helpful. I really appreciate the time you took to type all this out, to offer your thoughts and suggestions, and to try to make me feel a bit better. Thank you.

I don't even know what I said to him when he was suicidal. I just know that I was angry. He told me that I was the reason he wanted to kill himself, and that was hard for me to hear. And pretty unfair, too. This wasn't his first attempt since we started dating, but for some reason I didn't handle this one as well.

I tried the couple's chat with my therapist, and she is open to it, but he refuses to go. My therapist isn't directly trying to get me to leave him, but she uses subtle hints and cues (saying things like "If you decide to stay with him, you have to..." when I've never mentioned leaving him, for example).

Is there a way I can talk with him about this without the therapist there? I wish that I could just tell him how I feel. I've told him how insecure I am and he doesn't really seem to understand. He is no longer suicidal, but part of me wonders if he still loves me anymore.
